description: Calorie Balance Dashboard - Display daily calorie balance (intake - burn) from Cronometer and Mi Band data with 7-day visualization and offline caching

userStories.title: Set up Cronometer OAuth authentication
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to establish OAuth flow with Cronometer API so users can securely authenticate and grant access to their food logging and metabolic data.
acceptanceCriteria: OAuth 2.0 flow implemented with Cronometer endpoints
Credentials securely stored in platform keychain (Android Keystore / iOS Keychain)
Token refresh logic handles expired tokens gracefully
Token persists across app restarts
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Fetch calorie intake and metabolic data from Cronometer
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to fetch daily calorie intake (food), BMR, and TEF from Cronometer API so these values populate the dashboard calculations.
acceptanceCriteria: Ktor HTTP client configured for Cronometer API
Parse response JSON into domain models: DailyIntake { date, totalCalories } and Metabolism { date, bmr, tef }
Handle API errors and rate limits gracefully
Fetch covers 7-day date range
Network calls are non-blocking (coroutine-based)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Bridge Health Connect (Android) and HealthKit (iOS) for Mi Band data
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to read NEAT and EAT from platform health APIs using expect/actual pattern so Mi Band data is integrated into calorie burn calculations.
acceptanceCriteria: commonMain: Define HealthDataSource interface with readActivityData(dateRange) method
androidMain: Health Connect integration reading NEAT and EAT
iosMain: HealthKit integration reading HKQuantityTypeIdentifierActiveEnergyBurned
Parse and map activity data to ActivityBurn { date, neat, eat }
Request appropriate permissions (Android: HEALTH_CONNECT_READ; iOS: Health read)
Handle permission denial gracefully
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement local caching for sync data
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to cache synced data locally so the dashboard works offline and provides fallback when API calls fail.
acceptanceCriteria: Define CacheDataSource interface for storing DailyIntake, Metabolism, ActivityBurn
Store latest successful sync for each data source with timestamp
Cache keyed by date range (7-day window)
Clear cache when user signs out
Retrieve cached data when fresh sync unavailable
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Create CalorieMath repository for balance calculation
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a centralized repository that computes daily calorie balance from all sources so the calculation logic is testable and reusable.
acceptanceCriteria: Function: computeDailyBalance(intake: DailyIntake, metabolism: Metabolism, activity: ActivityBurn) -> DailyBalance
DailyBalance model: { date, intake, burn, balance } where burn = NEAT + EAT + BMR + TEF
Handle missing data gracefully (e.g., if activity unavailable, show intake - (BMR + TEF))
Sealed class error type for invalid inputs
Unit tests covering edge cases (zero values, negative balance, missing components)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Build dashboard state holder with refresh logic
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a shared state holder that manages the dashboard's data pipeline so loading, errors, and cached fallback are coordinated.
acceptanceCriteria: StateFlow-based state holder: DashboardState { uiState, lastSyncTime, errorMessage, selectedDateRange }
uiState sealed class: Loading | Success(data) | Error(message)
Manual refresh function triggers Cronometer + Health API calls in parallel
On API failure: fall back to cached data, set error message visible in UI
Track last successful sync timestamp from each source
Sync logic is main-safe (uses Dispatchers.Default for computation)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Display 7-day calorie balance chart
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see my daily calorie balance over the last 7 days in a clear chart so I can spot trends.
acceptanceCriteria: Bar or line chart showing balance for each day (positive = surplus, negative = deficit)
X-axis: date labels (Mon, Tue, etc.)
Y-axis: calorie values with zero line marked
Positive bars colored green, negative red
Responsive layout on phone and tablet

Picker allows selecting start date; automatically shows 7-day window

Shows: Intake (from Cronometer), NEAT, EAT (from Health), BMR, TEF

userStories.title: Handle and display missing data scenarios
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the dashboard to handle cases where one data source is unavailable so the app doesn't crash and users see partial data where possible.
acceptanceCriteria: If Cronometer unavailable: show Health data only (NEAT + EAT + BMR estimate)
If Health data unavailable: show Cronometer data only (intake, BMR, TEF; no activity)
Show warning banners for missing data (e.g., 'Activity data unavailable')
Display best-effort balance with caveat message
Unit tests cover all missing-data scenarios
